$description: Usage rules for the Editorial-Technical system. `rules` are enforced by `npm run audit:design` (scripts/audit-design-system.mjs). `guidelines` cannot be checked mechanically; follow them anyway. Tokens live in tokens.json. Changing this file changes the design system: do it only on Josh's request, never to make a failing audit pass.

hardcoded-token-color.why: A literal copy of a token value doesn't change when the token does, and a literal accent won't follow the surface onto ink.
hardcoded-token-color.fix: Use the token: a Tailwind class (text-ink, bg-paper, border-line, text-accent) or the custom property (var(--ink), rgb(var(--accent-rgb) / .2)). SVG presentation attributes can't take var(); use a class (fill-ink) or currentColor.

off-palette-color.why: Colors outside tokens.json are how second navies and warm near-blacks crept in.
off-palette-color.fix: Pick the nearest token. If the design really needs a new color, that is a design-system change: ask Josh, then add it to tokens.json, site.css and tailwind.config.mjs together.

default-palette-class.why: Tailwind's default palette (blue-500, gray-200, white, black) is still compiled because the config uses theme.extend, so these classes work but sit outside the system.
default-palette-class.fix: Use system colors: white → paper or raised, black → ink, gray-* → ink-muted / line, blue-* → accent.

legacy-color-class.why: Pre-rebrand names (navy, plum, coral, cream, sage, sky, charcoal, sunset, lemon) are aliases kept so old markup renders. New uses spread the confusion.
legacy-color-class.fix: Use the token named by replaceWith in tokens.json (navy/plum/charcoal → ink, coral → accent, cream → paper, sage/sky → ink-muted).

arbitrary-value.why: One-off Tailwind values (text-[0.6875rem], tracking-[-0.055em], rounded-[4px]) bypass the type scale and spacing that the primitives encode.
arbitrary-value.fix: Use the Heading / Text primitives or a standard Tailwind step (rounded-[4px] is just `rounded`). Arbitrary values belong only in the primitives listed in allowArbitraryValuesIn.

font-family.why: Font stacks are tokens. A literal family name skips the Astro font loader and its fallbacks.
font-family.fix: Use a font utility (font-sans, font-serif, font-mono) or var(--font-hanken) / var(--font-fraunces) / var(--font-geist-mono), or `inherit`.

restricted-font.why: The script face is the wordmark only (see restrictedTo in tokens.json).
restricted-font.fix: Use the Logo component; set any other text in font-sans or font-serif.

legacy-prop-value.why: Component props still accept pre-rebrand tone names for back-compat. They all map to the same few colors, which makes the intent unreadable.
legacy-prop-value.fix: Use the canonical value given in the message.

forbidden-prop-value.why: The prop value is valid TypeScript but a confirmed design decision rules it out.
forbidden-prop-value.fix: See the reason in the message.

token-sync.why: site.css and tailwind.config.mjs both implement tokens.json. If they disagree, the same token renders two ways depending on whether CSS or a utility class is used.
token-sync.fix: Change all three in one commit. Every Tailwind color/font key must map to a token, and every token's cssVar / tailwind value must match. Never baselined.

Section.purpose: Full-width page band. Sets the surface; the accent follows it automatically.

forbidden.surface-warm: surface-warm is for small inline callouts only. Full-section tan washes were retired on 2026-08-25.

Heading.purpose: Every heading. `level` sets the semantic tag and `visual` sets the size, so the visual hierarchy never breaks the document outline.

Text.purpose: Body copy on the type scale.

exceptions.reason: The demo palette is content: visitors swap accent hues to watch a token propagate.
Build-time generator for hand-drawn wireframe SVGs. Its colors and type are artwork, not interface.
Source sheets for case-study wireframe artwork, which depict client products in their own palette.
Overrides specific colors emitted by the Shiki code theme, so it has to match those literals.

guidelines.rule: There is exactly one accent hue. Don't add a second highlight color, gradient, or 'candy' palette for variety; hierarchy comes from type weight, size and the serif italic.
Don't reach for bg-raised white cards with shadows to group content. Case studies use hairline columns and panels (border-line) on paper; the small Berxi-style testimonial is the model.
surface-warm appears only on small inline callouts, never as a Section tone or full-width wash.
Interactive islands must look like the site, not third-party widgets: navy accent plus in-key editorial hues, the site's type and controls.
Case-study artwork goes in a sibling <Container width="wide">, never inside .case-layout (the sticky rail paints over it). No nested scroll regions anywhere.
The homepage carries no 'Shipped at' client-logo or client-name band. Don't propose one.
ink-faint (text-ink-faint, Text tone="faint") is for glyphs and separators only, never words a reader has to read.
site.css owns global classes (.rule, .measure, .mono-label, …). Don't redefine them in a scoped <style>; scoped styles also don't reach DOM created at runtime, so pre-render and toggle instead.
/style-guide/ renders the system. A new pattern isn't part of the system until it appears there and in src/lib/component-catalogue.ts.
